title: Agentic Delivery — Review Me, Review Me Not, Review Me

steps.title: Welcome to the Lab
steps.instruction:
Welcome to the Review Me, Review Me Not, Review Me lab. You will prepare a disposable repository for autonomous work, build a durable handoff packet, transfer a local plan to Copilot cloud agent, and bring the resulting pull request through CodeQL remediation and human review.

This is a challenge lab. Complete it in the disposable repository prepared before class, not in a production repository.

steps.title: Inventory the Repository
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Explorer. Identify the runtime manifest, dependency lock file, test directories, .github configuration, and any existing agent instructions.

Challenge: decide which context exists only on your machine and which context is durable enough to reach a cloud agent.

steps.title: Verify the Local Baseline
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Run the repository's normal dependency installation, build, test, and lint commands.

Record the exact successful commands. If the baseline is already failing, stop and resolve that failure before delegation. A cloud agent cannot distinguish inherited failures from regressions without evidence.

steps.title: Choose the Execution Surface
steps.instruction:
Classify the prepared task:
• Stay local if requirements are still changing
• Use a background agent if the work is isolated but needs local resources
• Use a cloud agent if scope, context, and validation are durable

For this challenge, identify what must be clarified before the task qualifies for cloud delegation.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the sidebar and terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Explorer: Ctrl+Shift+E
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Create a Readiness Audit
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Explorer. Create docs/handoff.md in the disposable repository.

Start with a # Repository readiness section. Record whether the repository has deterministic dependencies, documented commands, fast tests, clear instructions, bounded network access, and a task small enough for one cloud session.

steps.title: Resolve the Highest-Cost Gap
steps.instruction:
Choose the readiness gap most likely to waste a cloud session. Fix it now or document the exact remediation required before delegation.

Prioritize setup and validation failures over prompt wording. A deterministic command is stronger context than an instruction that asks the agent to guess.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the sidebar for you.

For future reference:
• Explorer: Ctrl+Shift+E

steps.title: Create Cloud Setup Steps
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Explorer. Create .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml and add one job named copilot-setup-steps.

Use least-privilege permissions. Install dependencies deterministically, then run the fastest command that proves the environment is usable. Use the repository's actual runtime and commands rather than copying the slide unchanged.

steps.title: Make the Workflow Testable
steps.instruction:
Add workflow_dispatch and a path-filtered trigger so the setup workflow can be validated before an agent depends on it.

Confirm the workflow is intended for the repository default branch. The cloud agent does not use this setup file until it is present there.

steps.title: Run the Setup Commands Locally
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Run the same install and validation commands used by your setup workflow.

Challenge: remove assumptions about cached dependencies, global tools, local services, or uncommitted files. The commands must work in a fresh environment.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the sidebar and terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Explorer: Ctrl+Shift+E
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Draft the Handoff Packet
steps.instruction:
Open docs/handoff.md and add these sections:
• # Objective
• ## Relevant context
• ## Acceptance criteria
• ## Validation
• ## Constraints and non-goals

Write one observable objective. Keep the task within one repository, one branch, and one pull request.

steps.title: Stress-Test the Handoff
steps.instruction:
We've opened Copilot Chat. Ask a local agent:

Review docs/handoff.md as an autonomous cloud agent. Identify missing context, ambiguous acceptance criteria, unavailable dependencies, and requirements that cannot be validated from this repository. Do not implement the task.

Use the response to tighten the packet rather than adding broad narrative.

steps.title: Prove the Packet Is Complete
steps.instruction:
Confirm that every acceptance criterion maps to a command, test, scan, or observable pull-request result. Add explicit security boundaries and non-goals.

Run Check Mission Progress when the packet is ready.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the Chat panel for you.

For future reference:
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Shift+I

steps.title: Start with the Plan Agent
steps.instruction:
We've opened Copilot Chat. Start a new local session and select the Plan agent. Enter:

Read docs/handoff.md and inspect the repository. Produce a file-level implementation plan. Map every acceptance criterion to a validation step. Ask about unresolved decisions instead of making assumptions.

steps.title: Challenge the Plan
steps.instruction:
Review the plan before implementation:
• Does it remain inside the declared scope?
• Does it name the files likely to change?
• Does it account for tests and security constraints?
• Can every completion claim be checked?

Resolve ambiguity in the local session while you are available to answer questions.

steps.title: Create the Handoff Point
steps.instruction:
Ask the Plan agent to summarize the approved plan and validation strategy. Do not begin implementation locally.

The task is ready to move when the plan can be executed without relying on unsaved files, local-only services, or unstated decisions.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the Chat panel for you.

For future reference:
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Shift+I

steps.title: Transfer the Session
steps.instruction:
We've reopened Copilot Chat. Return to the approved Plan session. From the implementation control, select Continue in Cloud and choose Copilot cloud agent.

Confirm the target repository before starting. The full chat context transfers, but unsaved files and local runtime state do not.

steps.title: Confirm the Cloud Task
steps.instruction:
Before sending, make sure the cloud session can read docs/handoff.md and the required setup workflow from committed repository content.

If Continue in Cloud is unavailable, verify your Copilot policy and repository eligibility. Do not replace this exercise with a local Chat simulation.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the Chat panel for you. The cloud session continues remotely.

For future reference:
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Shift+I

steps.title: Inspect the Cloud Evidence
steps.instruction:
We've opened Copilot Chat. Filter the session list to cloud agents and open your active session.

Inspect the setup-step output, proposed plan, changed files, commits, and commands executed. Compare each item to docs/handoff.md.

steps.title: Intervene Only with Evidence
steps.instruction:
If the session drifts, give one specific correction tied to an acceptance criterion or security constraint. If setup fails, repair the setup layer. If the plan is fundamentally wrong, stop and return local.

When the implementation and validation evidence are ready, instruct the cloud agent to create a pull request if it has not already done so.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the Chat panel for you.

For future reference:
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Shift+I

steps.title: Open the Pull Request
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. From the disposable repository, run:

gh pr view --web

In GitHub, inspect the pull request checks and open any CodeQL or code-scanning alert. Follow the source-to-sink evidence before choosing remediation.

steps.title: Classify the Finding
steps.instruction:
In the browser, determine:
• Which scanner produced the alert
• The source, propagation path, and sink
• Whether the alert affects the pull-request branch
• Whether remediation belongs in the current implementation or a separate fix pull request

Do not dismiss an alert before understanding the data flow.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you. The GitHub pull request remains open in your browser.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Assign the Alert to Copilot
steps.instruction:
In the GitHub code-scanning alert, select Assign to Copilot. This starts a distinct cloud-agent session with the alert as task context.

If the control is unavailable, confirm that Copilot cloud agent, Copilot Autofix, and the required GitHub security license are enabled. Use the prepared recording for this step rather than simulating the feature locally.

steps.title: Review the Remediation Session
steps.instruction:
Observe whether the agent:
• Explores files beyond the reported line
• Explains the intended fix
• Reruns the original analysis
• Iterates after a failed validation
• Opens a draft pull request with evidence

Record anything the agent could not validate. Best-effort validation is not proof of correctness.

steps.title: Request a Focused Iteration
steps.instruction: If the fix is incomplete or overbroad, comment on the draft pull request and mention @copilot. Ask for one specific correction tied to the alert path, expected behavior, or a missing regression test.

steps.title: Inspect Every Gate
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Run:

gh pr checks

Confirm the status of tests, lint, code scanning, and any Code Quality checks. A passing security scan does not replace functional validation or human review.

steps.title: Review the Complete Diff
steps.instruction:
Run gh pr diff or inspect the diff on GitHub. Verify the acceptance criteria, regression tests, dependency changes, permissions, and network access.

Request Copilot code review if available, then compare its comments with the deterministic checks and your own review.

steps.title: Keep Human Approval Required
steps.instruction: Confirm that the repository ruleset requires appropriate checks and at least one accountable human approval. Copilot review comments and agent-generated fixes should inform the decision, not approve their own work.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Choose the Next Handoff
steps.instruction:
Decide whether the remaining work belongs in another cloud iteration or a local debugging session.

Return local when the task requires unavailable hardware, private test infrastructure, interactive debugging, or rapid experimentation. Stay in the cloud for a small, repository-contained correction.

steps.title: Return the Branch Local
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Check out the pull-request branch with:

gh pr checkout

Run the exact validation commands from docs/handoff.md. If you make a correction, push it to the same pull request so the security and review history remains coherent.

steps.title: Close the Loop
steps.instruction:
Compare the final evidence to the original objective:
• Acceptance criteria are met
• Local validation passes
• Cloud checks pass
• Security findings are resolved or explicitly documented
• Human review is complete

Stop before merge unless you are the authorized approver for this disposable repository.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Lab Complete!
steps.instruction:
Congratulations! You completed the local-to-cloud agent delivery loop.

You practiced:
• Choosing the correct execution surface
• Optimizing setup, context, validation, and security boundaries before delegation
• Building a durable handoff packet
• Transferring a local Plan session to Copilot cloud agent
• Supervising cloud work through observable evidence
• Routing a CodeQL finding into agentic remediation
• Returning the pull request to local validation and human approval

The key result is not that an agent wrote code. It is that execution moved across environments without losing intent, evidence, or accountability.
